{{Short description|Type of topological space}}
In [[mathematics]], in the realm of [[point-set topology]], a '''Toronto space''' is a [[topological space]] that is [[homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] to every proper subspace of the same [[cardinality]].

There are five homeomorphism classes of countable Toronto spaces, namely: the [[discrete topology]], the [[indiscrete topology]], the [[cofinite topology]] and the [[upper topology|upper]] and [[lower topology|lower]] topologies on the [[natural numbers]]. The only countable [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] Toronto space is the discrete space.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Bonnet | first = Robert
 | contribution = On superatomic Boolean algebras
 | location = Dordrecht
 | mr = 1261195
 | pages = 31–62
 | publisher = Kluwer Acad. Publ.
 | series = NATO Adv. Sci. Inst. Ser. C Math. Phys. Sci.
 | title = Finite and infinite combinatorics in sets and logic (Banff, AB, 1991)
 | volume = 411
 | year = 1993}}.</ref>

The '''Toronto space problem''' asks for an uncountable Toronto Hausdorff space that is not discrete.<ref>{{citation|title=Open problems in topology, Volume 1|first1=J.|last1=van Mill|first2=George M.|last2=Reed|page=[https://archive.org/details/openproblemsinto0000unse/page/15 15]|publisher=North-Holland|year=1990|isbn=9780444887689|url=https://archive.org/details/openproblemsinto0000unse/page/15}}.</ref>
